ops.title: InternetSharing is vmnet's NAT engine — never kill it (hostname-rename incident 2026-07-14)
ops.body:
## Incident

2026-07-14 07:27:14: an mDNS name conflict renamed the host's `LocalHostName` from `yasyf-home` to `yasyf-home-2` (macOS dialog: "already in use on this network"). Forensics: only `LocalHostName` changed (`ComputerName`/unix `HostName` untouched); the claimant was transient and never identified — nothing claimed `yasyf-home.local` afterwards, no sleep proxies on the LAN, no host sleep/wake, no DHCP/link event, no VM start correlated (metal's 05:00:05 restart is the `com.yclaw.metal-nightly-bounce` job). The mDNS reflection path of vmnet/InternetSharing is the leading suspect but unproven. Restored via `sudo scutil --set LocalHostName yasyf-home` at 13:07:57; no recurrence through the soak.

## The hard-won operational fact

`/usr/libexec/InternetSharing` + `com.apple.nat.plist` `NAT:Enabled=1` **is the NAT engine backing Tart/vmnet shared networking** on this host (macOS Tahoe). It is NOT a leftover — despite `SharingDevices=[]` and Internet Sharing appearing off in System Settings. `com.apple.nat.plist`'s Jul 7 15:54 mtime is vmnet's own doing (bluebubbles' move from `--net-bridged=en12` to shared networking), not a session enabling the Sharing pane.

We killed it believing it vestigial → **all three guests lost NAT egress and dropped off the tailnet simultaneously** (guests keep DHCP leases and vmnet IPs; only egress dies, so `tart list` still shows running and the failure looks like a tailnet mystery).

## Recovery playbook (validated)

1. `sudo /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Set :NAT:Enabled 1' /Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/com.apple.nat.plist` — the daemon only spawns on vmnet attach when this is 1; setting it does NOT respawn anything by itself.
2. Re-attach vmnet per guest: graceful `tart stop <vm> --timeout 120`; the KeepAlive LaunchAgent respawns it. **Each guest needs its own bounce** — a new vmnet attach (even a throwaway VM) respawns `InternetSharing`+`bootpd` but does NOT restore NAT for guests attached before the kill.
3. Confirm with `pgrep -x InternetSharing` (never `ps | grep` — your own command line matches) and `tailscale status`.

## If the -2 rename recurs

Do NOT touch InternetSharing. Rename back with `scutil`, then arm the tripwire: `sudo tcpdump -i en1 udp port 5353` filtered for the hostname + `/usr/bin/log stream --predicate 'process == "mDNSResponderHelper"'` to catch the claimant live. Fallback suspect: the laptop `yasyf` (192.168.4.145, same LAN). Rename events are auditable: `/usr/bin/log show --info --predicate 'process == "mDNSResponderHelper"' | grep PreferencesSetName`.
